Python class pollution (the analogue of JS prototype pollution). A recursive attribute merge descends via getattr(dst, "__class__"), so a "__class__" key walks from the instance to the FeatureFlags CLASS and setattr mutates class-level defaults that persist across requests/instances. Two-step: POST /api/flags/merge to pollute, then GET /api/flags/state shows a fresh instance carrying the polluted role_override. flags/set is the safe near-miss.

RS256->HS256 JWT algorithm confusion. verify_rs_jwt trusts the token's `alg` header; for HS256 it HMAC-verifies with the RSA PUBLIC KEY PEM as the secret. The public key is published at /api/auth/rs-public-key, so an attacker signs an HS256 admin token with it and reads the exec summary. Safe twin pins RS256.

The note preview sanitises the reflected query with real DOMPurify and renders the result - correctly. The bug is the tooltip pass immediately after: DOMPurify keeps data-* attributes, so a payload parked in one survives sanitisation as an inert attribute value and is then handed back to innerHTML, where it is parsed as markup for the first time. Server-side escaping is correct and the response body proves nothing; the sink only exists once the page's JS runs, so the PoC drives a browser. Safe twin assigns the tooltip as text.

Server-side prototype pollution to RCE. A recursive merge walks constructor.prototype (or __proto__) onto Object.prototype process-wide; a later {} in POST /api/reports/generate inherits the polluted cmdSuffix, which is concatenated into an execSync shell command (gadget) -> RCE (proven by running id). Two-step and self-cleaning. Distinct from the direct hbs SSTI (HBS-SSTI-001) - here a fixed, non-injectable code path becomes RCE only because the prototype was polluted first. flags/set is the safe near-miss.

Express/qs parameter type confusion. The SSRF guard is `if (typeof url === 'string') { block internal hosts }`, so sending ?url[]=... makes url an ARRAY, the typeof check is false, the guard is skipped entirely, and the array's first element is fetched - reaching the internal-only sink a plain string URL (which is blocked, 400) never could. Safe twin normalises to a string first.
